# Outer Hebrides

Explore islands that are rich in wildlife, history and tradition. Discover a magical place where time stands still.

## The Outer Hebrides at a glance

- Food & drink:
Stornoway black pudding, fresh seafood, island whisky and gin

- History & heritage:
The Lewis Chessmen, Calanais Standing Stones, Iron Age houses, brochs, Comunn Eachdraidh Nis Museum, Kisimul Castle, St Kilda, Harris Tweed, Gaelic

- Nature & outdoors:
Point and Sandwick Trail, Balranald Nature Reserve, Hebridean Way, cycling, hiking, sea kayaking, surfing, wild swimming

- Wildlife:
Puffins, whales, seals, eagles, otters, dolphins, bashing sharks, Eriskay ponies, Bird of Prey Trail


Map of Scotland

## What to expect in the Outer Hebrides

This chain of Atlantic islands stretches for around 130 miles along the north-west coast of Scotland, with each island offering a different experience. Walk amongst mountains in Harris and on sweeping beaches in Uist, travel south to Eriskay to see its rare pony breed or set sail for St Kilda to experience its spectacular history and wildlife. Discover a place where you can explore at a gentler pace, admire untouched landscapes, watch for whales breaking the surface of the sea, uncover thousands of years of history, and sample the Atlantic produce. The Outer Hebrides are captivating in every season, offering a unique experience each time you visit. It's easy to see why _[National Geographic](http://www.nationalgeographic.com/travel/slideshow/best-of-the-world-2025)_ included these islands on their list of best in the world.

> An island can be seen as bounded by the sea or as infinitely connected.
>
> Peter Mackay, Lewis-born poet

## Highlights in the Outer Hebrides

From ancient stories and close-up wildlife encounters to amazing local flavours and traditions, the Outer Hebrides offer a range of unique experiences that you will cherish forever. Discover the highlights that truly capture the spirit of the islands.

#### Explore the island’s ancient landscapes

Walk through a landscape where ancient stone circles, cairns and brochs rest quietly among rolling hills, lochs and machair. Visit places such as Ardvouray in Harris, where a Viking grave mound was unearthed revealing historical artifacts which are now on display in the British Museum. Nunton Chapel and its graveyard, on the west coast of Benbecula, is another incredible spot where you can see archaeological remains. Book a guided tour to learn how these sites continue to shape the islands’ landscape. Download the award-winning free augmented reality archaeology app [Outer Hebrides Unearthed](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/see-and-do/history/uist-unearthed).

[Archaeology in the Outer Hebrides](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/see-and-do/history/archaeology)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/12/07/dun-carloway-broch)

Dun Carloway Broch, Outer Hebrides

#### Taste the islands, from the shoreline to the smokehouse

Sample the delicious, freshly caught seafood, including scallops, langoustines, crab, lobsters and mussels. Why not try the salmon gently smoked in local smokehouses using traditional methods? Make sure you also enjoy the homemade goods and bakes produced across the islands, along with Stornoway black pudding, which is made with oats, onions and spices by local producers.

[Food & drink in the Outer Hebrides](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/food-and-drink)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/10/01/croft-36-harris)

Croft 36, Harris

#### Go on a boat trip to spot whales and dolphins

There is nothing quite like the thrill of a coastal adventure! Set sail from Stornoway’s harbour with Immerse Hebrides on their 2-hour whale and dolphin tour to spot a variety of marine life. From dolphins and porpoises to minke and pilot whales, keep your eyes peeled. You might even be lucky enough to see orcas! Explore the [Hebridean Whale Trail](https://whaletrail.org/) to discover the different areas where the different species roam.

[Discover incredible marine life in the Outer Hebrides](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/see-and-do/wildlife/whales-and-dolphins)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2024/07/30/orca.jpg)

A majestic Orca glides through the waters off the coast of Scotland.

© iStock / Karl Weller

#### Into the wild: visit St Kilda

Adventure to this remote archipelago in the Outer Hebrides surrounded by sea stacks, islets and with a rich variety of birdlife. It is the UK’s only dual UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to nearly 1 million seabirds, including the largest colony of Atlantic puffins. You can see fulmars and gannets perched on the rocks, as well as grey seals swimming in the water nearby. St Kilda boasts dramatic and spectacular scenery, not to mention a magical and unique location. The abandoned village of Hirta is a reminder of when island life thrived in the past.

[Discover the magic of St Kilda](https://www.nts.org.uk/visit/places/st-kilda?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23655713982&gclid=EAIaIQobChMIm4Wdj6ablgMVnJNQBh2Zozx6EAAYASAAEgKcb_D_BwE)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2024/09/23/aerial-view-of-st-kilda.jpg)

An aerial view of the archipelago of St Kilda

## What's on in the Outer Hebrides

Listen to the lyrical tones of Gaelic folk music underneath Lews Castle, or meet fellow wildlife enthusiasts as you spot dolphins, seals, whales and more off the coasts of the islands of the Outer Hebrides.

previousnext

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/03/07/shiant-islands)

### [Outer Hebrides Wildlife Festival](https://www.outerhebrideswildlifefestival.co.uk/)

Celebrate the Outer Hebrides rich natural wildlife with events, workshops, walks and much more.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2025/08/22/royal-national-mod)

### [Royal National Mòd](https://www.ancomunn.co.uk/)

The Western Isles welcomes the Mòd, for a celebration of Gaelic culture featuring music, drama, Highland dance, literature and sport.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/01/23/heb-celt-festival)

### [HebCelt](https://www.hebceltfest.com/)

This music festival takes place on the stunning Isle of Lewis in the Outer Hebrides and is a celebration of Gaelic music, culture and language.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2024/08/01/benbecula.jpg)

### [Eilean Dorcha Festival](https://www.edffestival.com/)

The family-friendly festival in the Outer Hebrides features a variety of live music ranging from DJ sets to raucous ceilidhs.

## See the Outer Hebrides through a new lens

Discover the Outer Hebrides through the eyes of visitors and locals. Follow their personal recommendations and uncover hidden gems to inspire your own trip.

## Discover your ideal location in the Outer Hebrides

#### Stornoway, Lewis

The largest town in the Outer Hebrides. Take a stroll along its beautiful harbour and explore lively cafés and independent shops. Enjoy a walk through the grounds of Lews Castle, sample the delicious seafood in one of its restaurants and get your toes tapping as you listen to live music in a cosy pub.

[Visit the Isle of Lewis](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/our-islands/lewis)

#### Tarbert, Harris

Explore a village surrounded by mountains and white sandy beaches. Visit the Isle of Harris Distillery, galleries and crofting communities or admire the beautiful beaches of Luskentyre and Seilebost.

[Adventure to the Isle of Harris](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/our-islands/harris)

#### Lochmaddy, North Uist

Explore this small coastal town by following the coastal paths and enjoy the rich wildlife that calls it home. Visit the Taigh Chearsabhagh Museum and Arts Centre or walk along one of the many beautiful beaches.

[Discover North Uist](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/our-islands/uist/north-uist)

#### Eriskay

This peaceful island is the perfect place to slow down and immerse yourself in remarkable stories. Walk along Princes’ Beach, where Bonnie Prince Charlie first stepped on Scottish soil, or find out more about the story behind Whisky Galore. Reconnect with nature and feel the island breeze as you spend some time outdoors with the native Eriskay ponies.

[Plan your trip to Eriskay](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/our-islands/uist/eriskay)

#### Castlebay, Barra

Admire one of the most fascinating harbour views in the Outer Hebrides, with Kisimul Castle rising from the water. Climb up Heaval to enjoy incredible views of Barra or follow the causeway to Vatersay. Don’t forget that you can also see a plane landing on a beach in Barra! It is a unique and beautiful experience.

[Uncover the Isle of Barra](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/our-islands/barra/barra)

## Uncover the heritage of Harris Tweed

Learn how wool is transformed into this world-famous cloth and take home a memento of your unforgettable trip to the islands.

[Find out how Harris Tweed cloth is produced](https://www.harristweed.org/the-process/)

## Trip ideas in the Outer Hebrides

Breathe in the fresh Atlantic air as you follow the coastline, see if you can spot eagles gliding through island landscapes or sample some of the island’s fresh, local produce. Follow these trip ideas and make the journey your own.

previousnext

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/07/05/luskentyre-sands)

### [The Hebridean Way](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/hebrideanway)

Walk or cycle this epic trail which takes you from Vatersay to the Butt of Lewis.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2024/05/16/isle-of-harris-distillery)

### [Eat Drink Hebrides Trail](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/food-and-drink/eat-drink-hebrides-trail)

Taste the best food and drink the islands have to offer.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/05/26/golden-eagle.jpg)

### [Bird of Prey Trail](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/see-and-do/wildlife/bird-of-prey-trail)

Follow this self-guided tour around 13 locations in the Outer Hebrides to see some of Scotland’s most iconic predators.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/05/10/bonnie-prince-charlie)

### [Bonnie Prince Charlie trail](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/see-and-do/history/bonnie-prince-charlie-trail)

Explore this unique part of Western Isles history by following in the footsteps of the “Young Pretender”

### Getting to the Outer Hebrides

Ferry

## Ferry

You can access the Outer Hebrides with a ferry from the mainland. Caledonian MacBrayne (CalMac) operates ferries from Oban, Mallaig, Uig and Ullapool, on Scotland's west coast.

[Visit the CalMac website](http://www.calmac.co.uk/)

[Travel to the Outer Hebrides by ferry](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/visitor-info/getting-to-the-outer-hebrides/by-ferry "Travel to Lewis and Harris by ferry")

There are numerous marinas in the Outer Hebrides, so why not travel by sail-boat?

[Discover more about sailing in the Outer Hebrides](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/see-and-do/sailing)

* * *

Flying

## Flying

Loganair operates most services to the Outer Hebrides, with airports at Stornoway, Benbecula and the Isle of Barra. You can fly directly from places like Glasgow, Edinburgh or Inverness. The journey time from Edinburgh to Stornoway is 1 hour 45 minutes from Inverness and 1 hour from Glasgow.

[Visit Loganair’s website for more information](https://www.loganair.co.uk/)

[Relevant information for travelling by plane to the Outer Hebrides](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/planning-your-trip/getting-here/flights)

* * *

Bus and coach

## Bus and coach

Travel around the Outer Hebrides by bus for just £2 for a single fare! This offer is open to locals and visitors alike, letting you discover more during your trip.

[Find out more with Stagecoach](https://www.stagecoachbus.com/promos-and-offers/north-scotland/highlands-2-single-fare-cap)

* * *

Driving

## Driving

If you're planning to drive around the Outer Hebrides, make sure you're familiar with the rules for [driving in the UK](https://www.visitscotland.com/travel-planning/driving).

There are several companies that offer car hire at Stornoway, Benbecula and Barra airports, as well as at selected ferry terminals and other locations across the islands. Vehicles are limited, particularly during the high season and at weekends, so book in advance to avoid any disappointment.

[Car hire in the Outer Hebrides](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/planning-your-trip/getting-about/car-hire "Car hire in the Outer Hebrides")

[Campervan/motorhome guide for the Outer Hebrides](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/planning-your-trip/motorhomes "Campervan/motorhome hire in the Outer Hebrides")

* * *

### Accessibility

The Outer Hebrides welcomes all visitors, offering accessible attractions, accommodation and travel options. All CalMac ferries are accessible, and airports can arrange support when needed. Beach wheelchairs are also available at locations on Barra, Uist, Harris and Lewis. Plan your trip and contact providers in advance.

[More information on accessible travel in the Outer Hebrides](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/accommodation/holiday-ideas/accessible-places)

[Find more accessible places on Euan’s Guide](https://www.euansguide.com/reviews/results/homepage-search-all,26994?sortField=reviewsSummary.avgOverallRating&sortDirection=desc&country=United+Kingdom&region1=Scotland&region2=Na+h-Eileanan+an+Iar&formatted_address=Na+h-Eileanan+an+Iar%2C+UK)

## FAQs

When is the best time to visit the Outer Hebrides?

### When is the best time to visit the Outer Hebrides?

May to September is a great time to visit the Outer Hebrides, with plenty of opportunities to explore the islands' spectacular beaches and unique Gaelic culture. However, each season offers its own distinct charm.

Spring (March–May): Take advantage of longer days to visit the St Kilda UNESCO World Heritage Site from late spring, when seabird colonies begin to return.

Summer (June–August): Make the most of the long daylight hours by taking a boat trip from Stornoway to spot whales, dolphins and porpoises.

Autumn (September–November): Sample the flavours of the Outer Hebrides, from freshly landed seafood to locally crafted whisky at the Isle of Harris Distillery.

Winter (December–February): Experience the Outer Hebrides at a slower pace, with stargazing opportunities and the chance to discover heritage attractions such as the Calanais Standing Stones with fewer visitors.

* * *

How long should I stay in the Outer Hebrides?

### How long should I stay in the Outer Hebrides?

Allow at least a week to explore the islands of Lewis and Harris and Uist, but staying even longer lets you slow down and really get to know the islands. Head south to the lesser-known islands of Eriskay, Barra, Vatersay and more.

* * *

Where can I stay in the Outer Hebrides?

### Where can I stay in the Outer Hebrides?

There's a wide variety of options available, including self-catering accommodation, small hotels, cottages and hostels as well as campsites and glamping pods.

[Find your perfect place to stay in the Outer Hebrides](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/accommodation)

* * *

What food & drink can I enjoy in the Outer Hebrides?

### What food & drink can I enjoy in the Outer Hebrides?

The islands are famous for their seafood, particularly scallops, crab, langoustines, Hebridean salmon and lobster. There are many smokehouses where they still use traditional methods to prepare smoked fish such as salmon, trout, kippers and mussels. The Stornoway black pudding is a local speciality, and it is served in many restaurants.

And let’s not forget about whisky and gin. Tour one of the distilleries, meet the people behind the production process, and learn about the unique flavours that give them the unique taste and make them so special.

[Discover the best of the Atlantic larder](https://www.visitouterhebrides.co.uk/food-and-drink)
